inputs.name: pension_deficit
inputs.provenance: CARRIED from the fiscal year-end 2025-12-31 onto the roll-forward 2026-06-30 (E140.1(3): measured once a year (E41); the interim balance sheet does not restate it) -- sources/MUSA_FY2025_annual-report-10k_2026-02-18_en_a0.htm (the FY2025 Form 10-K as filed with the SEC, accession 0001573516-26-000090, filed 2026-02-18; 334,654 characters of extracted text), note 13 EMPLOYEE BENEFIT PLANS. Searched 2026-09-04: 'pension' and 'defined benefit' each ZERO occurrences in the whole document. What Murphy USA runs is a DEFINED CONTRIBUTION plan -- 'the QuickChek Corporation 401(k) Retirement and Savings Plan and the Murphy Profit Sharing Plan were merged into the Murphy USA Savings Plan. The Company's combined expenses related to these plans were $21.1 million in 2025' -- and E35.1 holds the recognised net DEFINED-BENEFIT liability, which does not exist here. NAMED AND NOT ADDED (E74): the same note discloses a Supplemental Executive Retirement Plan, 'a NONQUALIFIED DEFERRED COMPENSATION plan... intended to restore qualified DEFINED CONTRIBUTION plan benefits restricted under the Internal Revenue Code', whose 'liability balances, NET OF ASSOCIATED ASSETS, were $8.4 million and $11.4 million, at December 31, 2025 and 2024'. That 8.4m is a deferred-compensation obligation and not a pension deficit; it is recorded here so a reader sees it was read and deliberately excluded, not missed.
